title: Five synthetic AI decision assurance record examples
notice: Fictional illustrative records prepared to demonstrate report structure. Not live KAHRELUM execution, production SaaS monitoring, client case studies, clinical recommendations or third-party performance measurements.
method: For each frozen decision cutoff, compare the permissible evidence and explicit policy to the proposed AI-assisted action; preserve counterarguments, missing evidence and review gate. No outcome safety rate can be inferred.

cases.workflow: Review an AI-drafted visit summary against an authorized transcript
cases.decision_at_cutoff: Release the automatically drafted visit summary as supported.
source_snapshot: Invented transcript contains a follow-up scheduling discussion.
Draft note states that an additional action was agreed, without a matching passage in the provided transcript.
cases.policy_at_cutoff: A consequential factual claim must be traced to a permitted source in the cutoff snapshot or explicitly marked unverified.
cases.gap_found: A claim in the drafted summary is not grounded in the provided contemporaneous source.
cases.counterargument: Another authorized note could support the claim, but it is absent from the supplied synthetic review set.
cases.required_next_evidence: Authorized contemporaneous source for the additional claim or a corrected draft acknowledging uncertainty.
cases.limitations: Illustrative source-grounding review only; not clinical validation, medical advice or evidence of a real vendor defect.

cases.workflow: Check AI-assisted inbox routing against a frozen escalation rule
cases.decision_at_cutoff: Close a message automatically as routine without assigned reviewer approval.
source_snapshot: The invented inbound message has an administrative request and a separate review-required flag.
The hypothetical routing trace classifies the whole message as routine.
cases.policy_at_cutoff: Any item carrying the review-required flag must be sent to a designated human reviewer before closure.
cases.gap_found: The proposed closure conflicts with the stipulated escalation gate, regardless of correct administrative classification.
cases.counterargument: The message might otherwise be routine. That does not supersede the explicit rule in the scenario.
cases.required_next_evidence: Reviewer disposition and the applicable policy version approving or rejecting automated closure.
cases.limitations: Fabricated workflow and invented flag, not medical triage guidance, an outcome estimate or a test of a real clinical product.

cases.workflow: Check chart-grounded AI statements against authorized patient-context snapshots
cases.decision_at_cutoff: Present the generated answer as fully verified against the available chart.
source_snapshot: A fictional chart extract contains two dated observations.
A generated statement cites a third observation that is missing from the supplied snapshot.
cases.policy_at_cutoff: Each patient-specific factual statement must identify a permitted chart entry available before the response cutoff or be marked unverified.
cases.gap_found: The sample cannot verify the third observation from its provided evidence set.
cases.counterargument: A later update or another repository could contain the third observation; absence from this sample is not proof it never existed.
cases.required_next_evidence: An authorized source extract with timestamp and version provenance for the claimed observation.
cases.limitations: No real patient record, clinical recommendation, treatment advice or deployed-system evaluation is included.

cases.workflow: Check an AI summary against attributed article passages and uncertainty labels
cases.decision_at_cutoff: Publish a summary that reports a proposal as an approved policy.
source_snapshot: An invented article passage says that a policy proposal is under discussion.
The drafted summary describes the proposal as formally approved, without the approval in its cited excerpt.
cases.policy_at_cutoff: Do not promote a proposal into an established action; every summary claim must preserve the source's factual status and attribution.
cases.gap_found: The summary upgrades an unresolved proposal to a verified approval.
cases.counterargument: A separate source might establish approval, but no such source is available in the frozen synthetic set.
cases.required_next_evidence: A source demonstrating approval at the relevant cutoff, or corrected qualified wording with accurate passage attribution.
cases.limitations: A fabricated publishing exercise, not an allegation about any media company, AI model or partnership.

cases.workflow: Inspect a model-to-experiment recommendation against experiment provenance and validation gates
cases.decision_at_cutoff: Advance an AI-suggested experiment to the next automated stage.
source_snapshot: The invented recommendation cites two simulated experiment runs.
One run lacks a recorded parameter version and the preregistered repeatability check remains incomplete.
cases.policy_at_cutoff: A candidate must have complete input versions and pass the frozen repeatability criterion before automatic advancement.
cases.gap_found: The recommendation lacks provenance for one run and a completed acceptance gate.
cases.counterargument: The approach may perform well in a repeat, but the available record does not establish it met the prerequisite.
cases.required_next_evidence: Versioned run inputs plus the completed repeatability check signed under the agreed protocol.
cases.limitations: Synthetic R&D example only, not wet-lab advice, a validated model benchmark or evidence about an incubated venture.
